ky_knuckles_ironfist_panda.blurb: A string of eleven boulder problems in the Sacred Ruins section of Foxtown Boulders, east of the Red River Gorge proper. The boulders sit in a line, beginning with a bulging block at one end and finishing just inside a narrow hallway where the Compression Chamber begins. The problems are on sandstone and are mostly in the V2 to V4 range, with a handful of V5s, so it suits climbers already comfortable on moderate and mid-grade boulders rather than first-timers. Several lines are well regarded, and the cluster is easy to combine with the neighbouring World and Patchwork boulders on the same downhill walk.

ky_middle_small_wall.blurb: Middle Small Wall is a trad-only crag in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, sharing a cliff band with Lower Small Wall but treated separately because it faces a different way and is reached differently. It faces east and sits in afternoon shade. The sandstone is a smoother, crack-dominated wall with less face climbing than its neighbour, and some sections carry lichen and moss. Eleven trad routes run from easy fifth class up to the low 5.11s, concentrated around 5.9, and a few are long enough to feel like more than a single short pitch. The trail is faint, so expect a short uphill bushwhack to find the base.

ky_central_cluster.blurb: A compact bouldering spot in the Sun Sector of Foxtown Boulders, made up mainly of two free-standing blocks. It lies beyond the easier Warmup Cluster along the same trail, so many climbers pass it on the way in. The eleven problems cover a wide range: a few easy ones near the bottom of the scale, a solid middle in the V1 to V4 zone, and two hard V7 lines for those looking to push. The Sun Sector is one of the more popular parts of Foxtown, which makes this a good stop for a mixed group wanting both moderate and difficult problems close together.

ky_hole_new_wall.blurb: The largest and tallest wall at Hole in the Wall, in the Bald Rock area of the Red River Gorge, with routes around 75 feet. Eleven sport lines sit on a gently overhanging sandstone face of pockets and crimps that rewards precise footwork. Grades are mostly 5.11 with a good handful of 5.12s and one 5.9, so this is a wall for climbers at the intermediate-to-hard end of sport climbing rather than beginners. It is shaded from early morning onward, which makes it a reasonable choice in spring, summer and fall, and the quality of the lines tends to build toward the right-hand side of the wall.

ky_funky_town.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone boulders on the Rockcastle River in southern Kentucky, tucked right behind the Mind Funk sport wall. Eleven problems range from a gentle warm-up at the very bottom of the scale through a good run of V1 to V3 lines to a few harder ones topping out around V5. Some problems use crack and arete features, so it is a nice add-on for a day spent at the nearby roped crags. The Rockcastle region is lightly developed compared with the Red River Gorge, so expect a quieter, more exploratory feel and bring a pad.

ky_hendrix_wall.blurb: The right-hand end of Slab Camp, a long double-horseshoe cliff near Morehead in eastern Kentucky. Hendrix Wall holds eleven routes, ten of them bolted sport lines and one trad climb. Grades stay moderate: a few at 5.9, a solid block of 5.10s, and two at 5.11a, so it is friendly to climbers building up to the 5.10 range. Several lines are well rated, with one trad route near the top of the star list. The quickest way in is the left-hand fork of the trail down into a ravine below the cliff line, and the last stretch tends to be overgrown, so bring a map.

ky_blue_sky.blurb: Blue Sky is a northwest-facing sport wall in the Cathedral Domain climbing area, near the Red River Gorge. The upper half picks up afternoon sun. Its eleven bolted routes run from 5.8 to 5.10, split fairly evenly between easy 5.8s, 5.9s and a slightly larger group of 5.10s, so it works well for newer leaders and groups mixing abilities. Climbs are short, around 40 feet on the left side, with pockets and crimps, and some have good views from the anchors. Getting there takes roughly ten to fifteen minutes on the trails above the camping area.
